svg.text: Longer reports are wider, not padded
273 first-look reports: how long each is against how many of the twelve kinds of evidence it cites. One panel per
firm, because the firms sit at different places on both axes.
The relationship holds inside every firm — r from +0.19 to +0.79. Length buys range, not repetition.
Pooled across all six it reads +0.29, which is an artefact: between-firm spread swamps the slope inside each.
a separate and weaker finding — Muddy Waters first reports that became campaigns are the longer ones
Evidence kinds are the twelve probes in corpuslib, so this counts what a report declares. Lines are medians of reports in a word band, drawn only where a band
holds three or more — not a fitted line, because the relationship flattens once a report cites most of the twelve. 10 reports run past 26k words and sit on
the right edge of their panel.
